*   **Output:** A rank-reduced approximation $\tilde{\mathcal{A}}$ represented by truncated factor matrices $\mathbf{U}^{(n)}_k \in \mathbb{R}^{I_n \times K_n}$ and a truncated core tensor $\mathcal{B}_k \in \mathbb{R}^{K_1 \times K_2 \times \dots \times K_N}$.
The $n$-th factor matrix $\mathbf{U}^{(n)}$ has dimensions $I_n \times R_n$.
Columns correspond to principal components (basis vectors) ordered by importance (variance explained).
*   **Core Tensor:** Stored as an $N$-dimensional array of size $R_1 \times R_2 \times \dots \times R_N$.
*   Form the truncated matrix $\mathbf{U}^{(n)}_k$ containing only these columns.
*   Extract the sub-block of $\mathcal{B}$ defined by the indices $1 \dots K_1$ along mode 1, $1 \dots K_2$ along mode 2, ..., $1 \dots K_N$ along mode $N$.
*   Form the truncated core tensor $\mathcal{B}_k$ of size $K_1 \times K_2 \times \dots \times K_N$.
*   **Target Ranks $(K_1, \dots, K_N)$:** The desired reduced dimensions.
*   **Initial Ranks $(R_1, \dots, R_N)$:** Determined by the initial Tucker decomposition.
Truncated Tensor Decomposition originates from the properties of the Tucker Higher-Order Singular Value Decomposition (HOSVD).
